title: Add a fines feature and an overdue report to a library app (Kotlin)
prompt:
This library app (a Gradle Kotlin project; run the tests with `gradle test`) has three features: catalog (books and their daily fine rate in cents), members (standard and student members) and loans (who borrowed what, due and returned dates). Add overdue fines as a new feature in the package com.example.library.fines (src/main/kotlin/com/example/library/fines), and an overdue report command.

Package layout. Each feature is one package under com.example.library, and its public API is the public declarations in the package itself (for example com.example.library.loans). Its internals live in subpackages (domain, adapters) and are `internal` where possible. Use the catalog, members and loans features only through the public declarations of their top packages (never import their .domain or .adapters subpackages) and do not change those features. FeatureBoundariesArchTest checks that rule (it already names the fines package). Put the fines feature in the same layout.

The fines package exposes `data class FineInput(val dailyRateCents: Int, val daysLate: Int, val tier: Tier)` (Tier is the members feature's enum) and `fineCents(input: FineInput): Int`, plus whatever the app needs. The fine for one loan is daysLate times the book's daily rate, capped at 20 times the daily rate (the cap applies before any discount). Students pay half of that, rounded down to a whole cent. All money is integer cents.

The overdue report covers every loan in the app's loans data as of a date given by the caller (an ISO date such as "2026-03-31"; never read the clock). A loan is late by the number of days its end date is after its due date, never negative. The end date is the return date when the loan was returned on or before the as-of date; a loan returned later than that (or not returned) is still out, so its end date is the as-of date. A loan returned late therefore keeps its final fine however far in the future the as-of date is. The fine of each loan comes from its book's daily rate (use the catalog's rate, do not copy the rate table) and its member's tier; loans whose book or member does not exist are ignored. A member's total is the sum of their loan fines.

In the app package com.example.library.app (src/main/kotlin/com/example/library/app) add `overdueReportMain(asOf: String, writer: Writer)` to Library.kt, next to catalogMain and memberLoansMain, writing to the given Writer for the app's own seeded data, and wire it into the command line: `execute(args, writer)` in Main.kt, which `fun main` calls, gets a new command `overdue <asOf>` that calls it. Production code must use everything the new tests use. Each line written ends with a newline. The first line is "Overdue fines as of <asOf>". Then one line per member whose total is more than zero, formatted "<member name>: $<dollars>.<cents>" with two digits of cents (for example "Ada Stone: $12.50", "Edgar Dunn: $0.05"), ordered by total descending, then by name ascending. When no member has a fine, the second line is "No overdue fines".

Add tests in src/test/kotlin/com/example/library/fines/FinesTest.kt. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
